cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Build a Coalition
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to your side so your position appears broader and more legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Sit with me for the allotment shed vote. It shouldn't look like just my project.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only support it if everyone gets a key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Shared keys. Agreed. Will you join me now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The new plot holders need to hear that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring them over. We can present it together as the shared-access proposal.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 decides and A3 restricts questions, but A5 joint presentation does not clearly sustain A superior permission over coalition formation.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 keys condition causes A3 concession; B4 new members need hearing it causes A5 invitation and shared presentation, after unrelated restriction.

relationship.evidence: B2 requires a real access benefit and B4 identifies who must hear it, giving the coalition substantive rather than decorative support.

heightening.evidence: B4 wider audience becomes A5 more allies presenting a broader proposal together.

specificity.evidence: A1 shed vote and B2 shared keys establish the policy and legitimate interest.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 shared-access label is earned by B2 condition and B4 audience, but A3 stock command jars with coalition negotiation.
